definitions.explanation: A child who has no siblings.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}です。
{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}だから{兄弟|きょうだい}がほしかった。
examples.english: Since I'm an only child, I wanted siblings.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}は{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}の{家庭|かてい}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Families with only children are increasing recently.

notes:
{一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ} refers to a child with no siblings. The っ{子|こ} suffix gives a colloquial, familiar tone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}で{育|そだ}つ: to grow up as an only child
- {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ}{政策|せいさく}: one-child policy (China)

CULTURAL NOTE:
With Japan's declining birth rate ({少子化|しょうしか}), {一人|ひとり}っ{子|こ} families have become increasingly common. There is a common stereotype that only children are spoiled ({甘|あま}やかされている) or selfish, though this is often inaccurate.

VARIANT:
{一人子|ひとりご} is a more formal/literary alternative.
